{
  "reframes": [
    {
      "bottleneck": "Testing one feature costs 150 sequential closed-loop rollouts (up to 300 steps each, every step waiting on a ~150 ms forward pass plus the next observation), so answering whether any feature controls contact-rich or deformable behavior means months of serial robot or simulator time; an unbatched rollout also leaves the GPU idle while the simulator steps.",
      "assumption": "That a feature's effect can only be measured as closed-loop task success: the unit of measurement is a 300-step episode in which each observation causally depends on the previous action.",
      "reframe": "Change what is measured: score each feature by its open-loop action-chunk divergence (L2/KL between steered and unsteered predicted actions) on recorded contact-rich frames. Recorded observations break the step-after-step dependency, so every (frame, feature) pair is independent and thousands of steered forward passes batch on one GPU; serial closed-loop rollouts are reserved for the few features the screen promotes.",
      "question": "On the existing 135-feature rigid-task sweep, what is the Spearman rank correlation between per-feature open-loop action-chunk divergence (measured on ~10k recorded frames) and the already-measured closed-loop success delta per feature?",
      "measure": "Recompute each of the 135 steers as batched forward passes over ~10k recorded task frames (~1.35M forward passes, 1-3 A100-days batched, zero new rollouts), rank features by divergence, and correlate against the published 150-rollout success deltas; the episode logs already exist, so this is pure GPU inference plus an afternoon of statistics.",
      "compute_after": "If the screen validates (rho >= 0.7), the cloth question becomes embarrassingly parallel: sweep all 520 SAEs x all features against a few hours of recorded cloth and dish-rack teleoperation in GPU-weeks instead of robot-years, spending serial closed-loop rollouts only on the top-k; each added GPU buys a linear increase in features screened per day.",
      "exact": "Delta_i = mean over frames of ||a_steer_i - a_base||^2 on the action chunk (KL over action tokens as robustness check); Spearman rho with bootstrap CI between Delta_i and the closed-loop delta across the 135 features; prospective confirmation: top-5 open-loop features get 25 real rollouts each on one towel-fold task (125 episodes, ~2 robot-days).",
      "expected": "High correlation on rigid tasks: features that do nothing closed-loop should perturb nothing open-loop, and the large reported effects (+9 to +21 out of 25; 39/40 to 0/40) should produce large divergences; expect the screen to discard >80% of features at under 1% of the rollout cost.",
      "fails_if": "Open-loop divergence does not rank closed-loop success (rho < ~0.3), which existing VLA evaluations suggest is possible: small per-step action shifts can compound or be corrected under closed-loop feedback, in which case recorded-frame screening is worthless and the sequential rollout dependency is real.",
      "closest_prior": "Documented open-loop vs closed-loop gaps for VLAs (open-loop L2 predicting closed-loop success poorly in OpenVLA-class evaluations); RLinf-VLA's batched rollouts (1.61-1.88x with 256 ManiSkill envs) is the closed-loop alternative this would beat; action-token prediction accuracy is already used as a cheap proxy during VLA training."
    },
    {
      "bottleneck": "The 20,250-episode answer was bought as 135 features x 150 rollouts at uniform precision; if most features are near-null, most episodes purchased no information, and the same waste scales to any future cloth sweep.",
      "assumption": "That the objective is a precise success estimate per feature (hence 150 trials for every feature), rather than a decision - is this feature worth testing on cloth, yes or no - or a ranking of the top few.",
      "reframe": "Change the objective from estimation to screening: run a sequential probability ratio test or successive halving over features, killing nulls after ~10 rollouts and concentrating budget near the decision boundary. Compute becomes an anytime resource that buys discrimination among top candidates instead of uniform confidence intervals over all 135.",
      "question": "Replaying the recorded outcomes of the completed 20,250 episodes: what fraction of the 135 features are correctly accepted or rejected at alpha=0.05 within <=20 rollouts under an SPRT, and does successive halving return the same top-10 features using <=30% of the episodes?",
      "measure": "Retrospective reanalysis only: implement SPRT (H0: delta=0 vs H1: |delta|>=0.2, alpha=beta=0.05) and successive halving on the logged per-episode success sequences, average over ~100 random episode orderings, and compare the selected feature set and episodes consumed against the full-data answer. Cost: hours of analyst time, no GPU, no robot.",
      "compute_after": "If the retrospective saving is >=3x, every future sweep inherits it: the same robot-week screens 3-10x more features, SAEs, or tasks, and the freed budget is what pays for the first contact-rich sweeps on real hardware.",
      "exact": "Per feature, replay episodes in shuffled order; record episodes-to-decision under SPRT and under successive halving with brackets at 10/30/90 rollouts; report median and 90th-percentile savings, false-accept/false-reject rates vs the full-data labels, and the rank correlation of the halving top-10 with the full-data top-10.",
      "expected": "Large savings: the reported effects are enormous (+9 to +21 out of 25, and 39/40 to 0/40 on ablation), so most decisions are statistically obvious within 10-20 episodes; expect >=70% episode reduction with an identical top-feature set.",
      "fails_if": "Most true effects are small (|delta| < 5 percentage points), so no early-stopping rule can separate them - but that itself would be the finding that steering effects are mostly negligible; also fails if outcomes drift over the sweep (non-i.i.d.), which inflates SPRT error rates and must be checked from the logs.",
      "closest_prior": "Wald's SPRT; Hyperband/ASHA and best-arm-identification bandits in hyperparameter search; adaptive-subsampling approaches in LLM evaluation (tinyBenchmarks, IRT-based efficient benchmarks) applying the same trick to expensive evals."
    },
    {
      "bottleneck": "The one proven parallelization route - batched GPU sim rollouts, 1.61-1.88x at 256 ManiSkill environments - is written off because steering effects in simulation are assumed not to match the real robot ('false for cloth'), leaving all contact-rich steering evaluation serial on real hardware.",
      "assumption": "That steering-induced deltas inherit the full sim-to-real gap of the task: because absolute cloth behavior is wrong in sim, the effect of clamping a feature must also be wrong, so sim cannot even rank features for the real robot.",
      "reframe": "Test transfer of the delta, not the behavior. SAE features live in the network's activation space and encode its largely real-data-trained priors; the sim gap may sit in the physics while the feature-to-action-delta pathway is a property of the weights. If steering deltas correlate sim-to-real even when absolute success does not, sim becomes a valid screen and the parallel infrastructure applies directly.",
      "question": "Across >=12 features with known real-robot effects on a rigid tabletop task, is the Spearman correlation between sim-measured and real-measured steering success-deltas >=0.7, and what is that correlation on one deformable task (towel fold)?",
      "measure": "Build sim mirrors of 2-3 already-published steered tabletop tasks (~1 engineer-week), run batched sim rollouts for ~12 features x 100 episodes (1,200 episodes, 1-2 A100-days at 256 envs), reuse the published real numbers for rigid deltas, and add ~6 features x 25 real rollouts on one towel-fold task (~150 episodes, 2-3 days on one DROID-class setup). Total about 2 weeks.",
      "compute_after": "If rigid deltas transfer (rho >= 0.7) and cloth shows even rho ~ 0.5, the entire interpretability sweep moves to batched sim: compute then buys orders of magnitude - 420k-rollout-scale sweeps over all 520 SAEs and many deformable tasks become GPU-weeks, with real rollouts spent only confirming promoted features.",
      "exact": "Select features spanning the observed real effect range (+9, +15, +21 out of 25, plus the top-4 general features whose ablation took 39/40 to 0/40); replicate each steer in a ManiSkill/Isaac mirror of the DROID tabletop setup; delta_i = success(steer_i) - success(base) per domain; Spearman rho with bootstrap CI across features, reported separately for rigid and cloth.",
      "expected": "Rigid-task deltas plausibly transfer since those tasks succeed in both domains; cloth is the genuine bet - even a moderate positive correlation justifies sim pre-screening with real confirmation, still a 10-100x episode saving over pure real sweeps.",
      "fails_if": "Even rigid-task steering deltas fail to correlate (rho < 0.3), meaning the intervention pathway itself is sim-sensitive; then sim screening is dead at any physics fidelity and the remaining routes are open-loop screening or fixing cloth simulation first.",
      "closest_prior": "RLinf-VLA (256 parallel ManiSkill envs, 1.61-1.88x) as ready infrastructure; the deformable sim-to-real gap documented in cloth simulation benchmarks; analogous to RL findings that method or policy rankings can transfer sim-to-real even when absolute scores do not - treatment-effect rather than performance transfer."
    }
  ]
}
